thread.title_full: Ex Searched PA Mom's Facebook 300+ Times Before Killing Her, Hiding Body Under Motel Bed: DA - NewsBreak

author: Jillian Pikora
title: Ex Searched PA Mom's Facebook 300+ Times Before Killing Her, Hiding Body Under Motel Bed: DA - NewsBreak
text:
By Jillian Pikora ,
14 hours ago
A Pennsylvania man who searched his ex-girlfriend's name on Facebook more than 300 times in the days before killing her, then carried her body into a motel room and hid it beneath a bed, has been convicted of first-degree murder, prosecutors announced.
Brian Kuchinka, of Port Allegany, was found guilty of first-degree murder in the killing of 28-year-old K-Leigh Hill-Nelson on Wednesday, Aug. 26, McKean County District Attorney Stephanie Vettenburg-Shaffer said.
Kuchinka had previously pleaded guilty to criminal homicide and abuse of a corpse, admitting he caused Hill-Nelson's death but disputing that he intentionally killed her. That left a judge to determine whether the killing amounted to first- or third-degree murder, voluntary manslaughter, or involuntary manslaughter.
The judge found it was first-degree murder.
Hill-Nelson was reported missing after she failed to arrive for her 10 p.m. shift at a Smethport nursing home on Feb. 21, 2025, according to prosecutors.
Witnesses had seen a visibly distressed woman believed to be Hill-Nelson on Water Street shortly before her shift, where Kuchinka's vehicle was later found abandoned. Residents near her workplace then reported hearing what sounded like a gunshot around 9:57 p.m. and seeing a car speed away.
Cellphone records and surveillance footage showed Kuchinka driving toward Hill-Nelson as she followed her normal route to work, then traveling closely with her after their phones converged, Pennsylvania State Police Trooper Whitney Boshart testified.
Video later showed Kuchinka in Hill-Nelson's vehicle. Her SUV was found at a closed Port Allegany restaurant with blood on the seats, floor, and steering wheel, prosecutors said.
Investigators also uncovered extensive activity involving Hill-Nelson's social media accounts.
Kuchinka searched Facebook for her more than 300 times over several days and repeatedly searched for a man she had recently reconnected with, according to Boshart.
Witnesses testified Kuchinka was known to access Hill-Nelson's accounts without permission. His phone was used to log into her Facebook account repeatedly in the days before her death, including the day she was killed.
Just hours before the murder, Hill-Nelson unfriended Kuchinka and changed her Facebook password, prosecutors said.
Her account was accessed again after she was dead.
Kuchinka had been staying at a motel after Hill-Nelson and her father evicted him from their home weeks earlier, according to the DA.
When officers went to his room while searching for Hill-Nelson the next day, they heard a gunshot. After an hours-long standoff, Kuchinka surrendered with a loaded handgun in his back pocket and a self-inflicted gunshot wound to his head that was not life-threatening, prosecutors said.
Officers entered the room and found Hill-Nelson's body, without clothing, beneath the bed. She had been shot in the head.
Surveillance footage showed Kuchinka carrying her lifeless body from her vehicle into the motel hours after she failed to show up for work, according to the DA.
Hill-Nelson was a 2015 graduate of Port Allegany High School and worked as a certified nursing assistant at Lakeview Healthcare & Rehabilitation Center in Smethport, according to her obituary published by Hartle-Tarbox Funeral Homes Inc.
She loved spending time with her son and family and was remembered as "a kind and caring soul" by those closest to her.
She left behind an 8-year-old son, her father, a brother, three sisters, and extended family.
A GoFundMe launched by her sister, Keiya Rupert, raised more than $15,000 from 148 donors — surpassing its $10,000 goal — to cover funeral expenses and establish a trust for Hill-Nelson's son.
"We are blessed to know K-Leigh has an army behind her, even those that never met her," Rupert wrote in an update to donors.
Vettenburg-Shaffer credited Boshart and the other officers involved in the investigation while acknowledging the verdict could not undo the family's loss.
"The family will be left to mourn K-Leigh for the rest of their lives," the DA said. "K-Leigh was a mother, daughter, sister, niece and friend and her absence will be felt by many people forever."
Anyone experiencing domestic violence can contact the YWCA of Bradford's crisis line at 1-888-822-6325.
